description: Schweinfurth's travels in the Bahr-el-Ghazal and the lands of the Niam-niam (1868–71) — the great German naturalist's exploration of the unknown Sudan.

title: The Heart of Africa, Vol. II
creator: Georg Schweinfurth
description: Schweinfurth's travels in the unexplored Sudan — the Niam-niam, the Monbuttoo, and the pygmies of the Congo forest.

title: A Voyage of Discovery to the North Pacific Ocean, and Round the World, Vol. III
creator: George Vancouver
description: The official account of Vancouver's survey of the Pacific Northwest (1791–95) — vol. III of the 1798 first edition.

title: A Voyage to Terra Australis, Vol. I
creator: Matthew Flinders
description: Flinders' circumnavigation of Australia in HMS Investigator (1801–03) — the voyage that named Australia.

title: A Voyage to Terra Australis, Vol. II
creator: Matthew Flinders
description: Flinders' voyage continued — the Porpoise shipwreck and six and a half years' imprisonment at Mauritius.

title: Narrative of a Journey to the Shores of the Polar Sea, 1819–22
creator: John Franklin
description: Franklin's overland expedition to the Coppermine River and the Arctic coast (1819–22) — the journey of starvation and endurance that made his name.

title: Voyages from Montreal
creator: Alexander Mackenzie
description: Mackenzie's voyages to the Arctic Ocean (1789) and across the Rockies to the Pacific (1793) — the first transcontinental crossing of North America.

title: The Naturalist on the River Amazons
creator: Henry Walter Bates
description: Bates' eleven years on the Amazon (1848–59) — the naturalist's classic that founded the study of mimicry.

title: The Lake Regions of Central Africa
creator: Richard Francis Burton
description: Burton's expedition with Speke to the great lakes (1857–59) — the search for the Nile's source and the discovery of Tanganyika.

title: First Footsteps in East Africa
creator: Richard Francis Burton
description: Burton's disguised pilgrimage to Harar (1854–55) — the first European to enter the forbidden city and live.

title: How I Found Livingstone
creator: Henry Morton Stanley
description: Stanley's 1871 expedition across Africa to Ujiji — 'Dr. Livingstone, I presume?' and the finding of the lost explorer.

title: The Congo and the Founding of Its Free State, Vol. I
creator: Henry Morton Stanley
description: Stanley's founding of the Congo Free State (1879–84) — the Emin Pasha relief expedition's prelude and the scramble for the Congo.

title: The Congo and the Founding of Its Free State, Vol. II
creator: Henry Morton Stanley
description: Stanley's Congo narrative continued — stations, treaties, and the making of the Free State.

title: Narrative of an Expedition to the Zambesi and Its Tributaries
creator: David Livingstone
description: Livingstone's Zambesi expedition (1858–64) — the Universities' Mission, the Shire highlands, and the discovery of Lake Nyasa.

title: A Voyage to the Pacific Ocean, Vol. I
creator: James Cook
description: The official account of Cook's third voyage (1776–79) — the search for the Northwest Passage and the discovery of Hawaii.

title: The Voyage of the Vega Round Asia and Europe, Vol. I
creator: Adolf Erik Nordenskiöld
description: Nordenskiöld's Vega expedition (1878–80) — the first transit of the Northeast Passage.

title: The Voyage of the Vega Round Asia and Europe, Vol. II
creator: Adolf Erik Nordenskiöld
description: The Vega expedition continued — wintering off Siberia and the triumphant return through Asia.

title: A Journey from Prince of Wales's Fort in Hudson's Bay to the Northern Ocean
creator: Samuel Hearne
description: Hearne's overland journey to the Coppermine River and the Arctic Ocean (1769–72) — the first European to reach the Arctic coast overland, with Matonabbee.

title: Report of the Exploring Expedition to the Rocky Mountains
creator: John C. Frémont
description: Frémont's report of the 1842 and 1843–44 expeditions — the 'Pathfinder's' survey that opened the Oregon Trail and California.

title: The Expeditions of Zebulon Montgomery Pike, Vol. I
creator: Zebulon Montgomery Pike (Elliott Coues, ed.)
description: Pike's journals of the 1805–06 Mississippi and 1806–07 southwestern expeditions, in Coues' definitive edition.

title: The Expeditions of Zebulon Montgomery Pike, Vol. II
creator: Zebulon Montgomery Pike (Elliott Coues, ed.)
description: Pike's southwestern expedition continued — across the plains, the Sangre de Cristos, and capture by the Spanish.

title: The Expeditions of Zebulon Montgomery Pike, Vol. III
creator: Zebulon Montgomery Pike (Elliott Coues, ed.)
description: Pike's expedition concluded — Santa Fe, Chihuahua, and the return through Texas; with the appendices.

title: The Oldest Code of Laws in the World
creator: Hammurabi (C. H. W. Johns, trans.)
description: C. H. W. Johns' landmark English translation of the Code of Hammurabi (c. 1754 BC) — 282 laws on commerce, family, labor and justice, the oldest substantially complete written legal code — with Johns' introduction on Babylonian law. Transcribed from the 1903 T. & T. Clark edition.

title: Ancient Laws and Institutes of England, Vol. I
creator: Benjamin Thorpe (ed.)
description: Vol. I of the Record Commission edition of the Anglo-Saxon dooms — the laws of AEthelberht, Alfred, Cnut and others — with facing-page English translation. The foundational source collection for early English law.

title: Ancient Laws and Institutes of England, Vol. II
creator: Benjamin Thorpe (ed.)
description: Vol. II of the Record Commission edition — the later Anglo-Saxon and Anglo-Norman legal texts, with Thorpe's glossary and indexes. Completes the great 1840 source collection of early English law.

title: The History of the Common Law of England
creator: Matthew Hale
description: Chief Justice Hale's posthumous history — the common law versus statute law, the Saxon and Norman roots of English law, the courts and their evolution. The first great historical account of the common-law tradition, staged from the 1713 first edition.

title: Bracton's Note Book, Vol. I: Introduction and Apparatus
creator: Henry de Bracton (F. W. Maitland, ed.)
description: Vol. I of Maitland's edition of Bracton's case notes — introduction and apparatus to the nearly 2,000 plea-roll cases (1217-1240) that underlie Bracton's De Legibus, the first great English law treatise.

title: Bracton's Note Book, Vol. II: Text
creator: Henry de Bracton (F. W. Maitland, ed.)
description: Vol. II of Maitland's Bracton's Note Book — the plea-roll cases themselves, the raw judicial material from which Bracton built his treatise on the laws of England.

title: Bracton's Note Book, Vol. III: Text
creator: Henry de Bracton (F. W. Maitland, ed.)
description: Vol. III of Maitland's Bracton's Note Book — the remaining plea-roll cases with indexes, completing the edition of the 13th-century case law behind De Legibus.

title: The Law of Nations; or, Principles of the Law of Nature
creator: Emer de Vattel (Joseph Chitty, ed.)
description: Vattel's 1758 classic of international law in Joseph Chitty's English edition with notes — the textbook of diplomacy and the law of nations, constantly cited by the American founders.

title: A Treatise on the Law of Obligations, or Contracts
creator: Robert Joseph Pothier (William David Evans, trans.)
description: Pothier's treatise on obligations — the French civilian foundation of modern contract law and the principal source of the Code civil's contract provisions — in Evans' 1806 English translation with introduction, appendix and notes on English law.

title: The Civil Law in its Natural Order, Vol. I
creator: Jean Domat (William Strahan, trans.; Luther S. Cushing, ed.)
description: Vol. I of Domat's rationalist restatement of Roman private law — 'the oracle of the civil law' — in Strahan's English translation as re-edited by Cushing: the bridge from Roman law to the Code Napoleon.

title: The Civil Law in its Natural Order, Vol. II
creator: Jean Domat (William Strahan, trans.; Luther S. Cushing, ed.)
description: Vol. II of Domat's Civil Law in its Natural Order — successions, obligations and the public law — completing Cushing's edition of Strahan's translation.

title: The Code Napoleon; or, The French Civil Code
creator: France (Commission of the Code Napoleon)
description: The 1804 Code civil in the 1827 English translation — the most influential civil code in history, the model for codes across Europe, Latin America and beyond.

title: Lectures on Jurisprudence; or, The Philosophy of Positive Law, Vol. I
creator: John Austin (Robert Campbell, ed.)
description: Vol. I of Austin's lectures — the command theory of law: sovereignty, commands, sanctions, the province of jurisprudence. The founding work of analytical jurisprudence, in Campbell's 5th edition.

title: Lectures on Jurisprudence; or, The Philosophy of Positive Law, Vol. II
creator: John Austin (Robert Campbell, ed.)
description: Vol. II of Austin's lectures — rights, persons, things, and the applications of the command theory across the divisions of law. Completes Campbell's 5th edition.

title: Lectures on Jurisprudence, Vol. III: Notes and Fragments
creator: John Austin
description: The posthumous third volume of Austin's Lectures — notes and fragments first published from his manuscripts in 1863, the sequel to The Province of Jurisprudence Determined.

title: Village-Communities in the East and West
creator: Henry Sumner Maine
description: Maine's six lectures on the village community as the primitive legal unit — India, Russia, England — extending Ancient Law's comparative method to property and the 'from status to contract' thesis.

title: Dissertations on Early Law and Custom
creator: Henry Sumner Maine
description: Maine's later essays — sovereignty, the king in early law, theories of primitive society, the natural state of mankind. The mature statement of his historical jurisprudence.

title: Commentaries on the Constitution of the United States, Vol. I
creator: Joseph Story
description: Vol. I of Justice Story's great commentary — the constitutional history of the colonies and states before 1787. The most cited American constitutional treatise of the 19th century, from the 1833 first edition.

title: Commentaries on the Constitution of the United States, Vol. II
creator: Joseph Story
description: Vol. II of Story's Commentaries — the legislature, the executive, and the powers of Congress under the Constitution.

title: Commentaries on the Constitution of the United States, Vol. III
creator: Joseph Story
description: Vol. III of Story's Commentaries — the judiciary, the states, amendments, and the forms of process. Completes the 1833 first edition.

title: Commentaries on American Law, Vol. I
creator: James Kent
description: Vol. I of Chancellor Kent's Commentaries — 'the American Blackstone': the law of nations, government, and constitutional law. The foundational American legal treatise, staged from the 1828 printing of vol. I.

title: Commentaries on American Law, Vol. III
creator: James Kent
description: Vol. III of Kent's Commentaries (2nd ed., 1832) — real property: feudal tenures, estates, and the American law of land.

title: A Treatise on the Constitutional Limitations which Rest upon the Legislative Power of the States of the American Union
creator: Thomas M. Cooley
description: Cooley's Constitutional Limitations (2nd ed., 1871) — the 19th century's leading treatise on due process, vested rights and the police power; the intellectual charter of American laissez-faire constitutionalism.

title: A First Book of Jurisprudence for Students of the Common Law
creator: Frederick Pollock
description: Pollock's introduction to legal theory for common-law students — the nature of law, the state, rights, duties and the sources of law. The standard English jurisprudence textbook of its generation.

title: The History of English Law before the Time of Edward I, Vol. I
creator: Frederick Pollock and Frederic William Maitland
description: Vol. I of Pollock and Maitland's History — the masterpiece of English legal historiography: the Anglo-Saxon age, the Norman conquest, and the making of the common law. 1895 first edition.

title: The History of English Law before the Time of Edward I, Vol. II
creator: Frederick Pollock and Frederic William Maitland
description: Vol. II of Pollock and Maitland's History — the doctrines of the common law to 1272: tenure, the courts, procedure, crime and tort. Completes the 1895 first edition.

title: English Law and the Renaissance
creator: Frederic William Maitland
description: Maitland's 1901 Rede Lecture — how the English common law survived the Renaissance reception of Roman law that transformed the Continent. The classic essay on England's legal exceptionalism.

title: A History of English Law, Vol. I
creator: William Searle Holdsworth
description: Vol. I of Holdsworth's monumental History (3rd ed., 1922) — the judicial system: the courts and their development. The standard reference history of English law.

title: A History of English Law, Vol. II
creator: William Searle Holdsworth
description: Vol. II of Holdsworth's History (3rd ed., 1922) — Anglo-Saxon and Norman law, the sources of English law.

title: A History of English Law, Vol. III
creator: William Searle Holdsworth
description: Vol. III of Holdsworth's History (3rd ed., 1922) — the medieval common law: the development of the courts and the legal profession.

title: The Geneva Bible (1560)
creator: William Whittingham and others
description: The Geneva Bible of 1560 — the first full edition of the Bible of the English exiles at Geneva (Whittingham, Coverdale, Goodman, Gilby, Sampson, Cole); the first English Bible with verse divisions, the Bible of Shakespeare and the Pilgrims. Complete Old and New Testaments with Apocrypha, from a 1560 printing.

title: The Great Bible (1539)
creator: Myles Coverdale
description: The Great Bible of 1539 — 'the Byble in Englyshe', the first authorized English Bible, prepared by Myles Coverdale under Thomas Cromwell and set up in every English parish; the revision of Matthew's Bible that the Geneva translators then revised in turn. Complete Old and New Testaments.

title: Matthew's Bible (1537)
creator: John Rogers (as Thomas Matthew)
description: Matthew's Bible of 1537 — John Rogers' compilation under the pseudonym Thomas Matthew, combining Tyndale's New Testament and Pentateuch with Coverdale's rendering of the rest; the pivotal bridge edition between Tyndale and the Great Bible, the first Bible printed in England under royal licence. Complete Old and New Testaments.

title: Biblia: Die gantze Heilige Schrifft Deudsch (Luther, 1545)
creator: Martin Luther
description: The Luther Bible of 1545 — 'Biblia: das ist: Die gantze Heilige Schrifft Deudsch, auffs new zugerichtet', printed by Hans Lufft at Wittenberg; the last edition overseen by Luther himself ('Ausgabe letzter Hand'), the translation that shaped the German language. Complete Bible in the original Early New High German.

title: Forerunners and Rivals of Christianity, Vol. 1: From 330 B.C. to 330 A.D.
creator: Francis Legge
description: Francis Legge's history of Christianity's forerunners and rivals — Vol. 1 (1915), covering the pre-Christian religious world: Alexander's conquests, the Alexandrian divinities, the origin of Gnosticism, and the pre-Christian Gnostics. Companion to the already-hosted Vol. 2 on the post-Christian Gnostic systems.

title: The Apostolic Tradition of Hippolytus (Easton translation)
creator: Hippolytus of Rome; translated by Burton Scott Easton
description: Burton Scott Easton's 1934 English translation — with introduction and notes — of Hippolytus of Rome's Apostolic Tradition (c. 215 AD), the earliest surviving church order, describing early Christian ordination, baptism, and eucharistic practice in detail. Public domain (Project Gutenberg).

title: Treaty of Westphalia (1648) — Treaty of Münster
creator: Holy Roman Emperor and King of France (plenipotentiaries)
description: The 1648 Treaty of Münster — the principal instrument of the Peace of Westphalia, ending the Thirty Years’ War. English translation.

title: Instrument of Government (1653)
creator: England (Council of Officers; drafted by John Lambert)
description: The 1653 Instrument of Government — England’s first codified constitution, establishing the Protectorate.

title: Edit de Nantes (1598) — Edict of Nantes
creator: Henri IV of France
description: The 1598 Edict of Nantes — Henri IV’s edict of religious toleration for French Protestants (French original).

title: Locke
creator: Samuel Alexander
description: Samuel Alexander's 1908 study of John Locke in the Philosophical Classics series.

title: Of God and His Creatures: An Annotated Translation (with some Abridgement) of the Summa Contra Gentiles
creator: Thomas Aquinas (Joseph Rickaby, trans.)
description: Rickaby's 1905 annotated English rendering of Aquinas's Summa Contra Gentiles, covering all four books (abridged): the obtainable complete public-domain English SCG.

title: Compendium Maleficarum
creator: Francesco Maria Guazzo (Montague Summers, trans./ed.)
description: Guazzo's 1608 witch-hunter's manual in Montague Summers's 1929 English translation: the classic early-modern demonology of witchcraft prosecution and its remedies.

title: Philosophie als strenge Wissenschaft
creator: Edmund Husserl
description: Husserl's 1911 programmatic essay 'Philosophy as Rigorous Science' (Logos, vol. I): the founding manifesto of the phenomenological movement. Extracted from the complete Logos I volume; German.

title: The Jesuit Relations and Allied Documents, Vol. 26
creator: Reuben Gold Thwaites (ed.)
description: Vol. 26 (Lower Canada) of Reuben Gold Thwaites's 73-volume edition of the Jesuit Relations (1896-1901): the foundational documentary corpus of the North American indigenous missions. Completes vols. 1-30.

title: The Institutes of Justinian
creator: Justinian I (J. B. Moyle, trans.)
description: Moyle's translation of Justinian's Institutes (1906 ed.): alternate English rendering to the Sandars 1874 translation already in the library.

title: Second Characters; or, The Language of Forms
creator: Anthony Ashley Cooper, Earl of Shaftesbury (Benjamin Rand, ed.)
description: Shaftesbury's Second Characters (ed. Benjamin Rand, 1914): the posthumous second series of the Characteristics, on art, aesthetics and the language of forms.

title: The Damnable Life and Death of One Stubbe Peeter, a Most Wicked Sorcerer
creator: Anonymous
description: The 1590 English pamphlet on Peter Stumpp (Stubbe Peeter), executed 1589 for murders, lycanthropy and witchcraft: the founding werewolf pamphlet of early modern England.

title: Textes philosophiques
creator: Léon Wieger
description: Wieger's 1906 French collection of Chinese philosophical and religious texts. French.

title: A Course of Lectures on Natural Philosophy, Vol. 1
creator: Thomas Young
description: Vol. 1 of Thomas Young's 1807 Course of Lectures on Natural Philosophy and the Mechanical Arts: the polymath's great physics lectures. Completes the set with Vol. 2 (already in the library).
